titleStmt.title: No. 924
The Secretary of State to the Embassy in Egypt

div.head:
No. 924
The Secretary of State to the Embassy in Egypt
div.p:
841. FYI Israel Amb informed Byroade that although Chairman EIMAC has appealed for immediate release Bat Galim and crew, IG has no indication so far Egypt has moved comply. Israel believes parties should respect implications MAC decisions as Israel respected UNTSO orders in past (Huleh Marshes and Banat Yaqub). Requested US assistance inside or outside UN on release Bat Galim and upholding SC resolution Sept 1, 1951. Byroade replied while
Dept has no definite indication GOE intention, expects Egypt would now probably release crew and vessel and make some provision compensation perishable cargo already sold. Believed Dept could be helpful this repect. Doubted Egypt prepared permit Bat Galim or other Israel flag ship transit Canal.

Asked how Amb envisaged further action in SC, Eban replied he imagined Council would note such action by Egypt with gratification and voice hope this prelude to general compliance by Egypt with SC resolution 1951.

Byroade stated no question US position on freedom transit principle and Dept would endeavor encourage Egyptian compliance, preferably outside UN. However, since case now in UN would “try say right things” in Council discussion. End FYI.

For Cairo: Embassy Cairo requested inform Foreign Office Dept believes Egyptian action releasing crew and cargo and compensating for perishable goods already sold will be beneficial to Egypt, particularly for effect action would have international opinion. If such action to have greatest impact, should be taken at once, before SC resumes consideration issue.

Concerning release of ship itself, in view Egyptian decision not pursue suggestion to refer question to ICJ, Dept sees no way in which Egypt can prevent ship from transiting Canal without being in violation SC resolution Sept 1, 1951 (Embtel 714 Nov 29). Believes Israel intends press issue eventually with additional test cases. Continue impasse will cause embarrassment United States and Egypt. Dept therefore hopes Egyptian decision re Bat Galim indicative intention relax restrictions generally on Israel shipping.
For USUN: If IsraelDel shows signs pressing for early SC meeting, suggest USUN seek delay matters in line Eban–Byroade conversation.

note.p: Sent also to New York; repeated to Tel Aviv and London.

Ambassador Caffery reported that the substance of the pertinent paragraphs of the Department’s telegram 841 were conveyed to the Egyptian Foreign Minister on Dec. 2. Fawzi stated that the matter of the crew and cargo would be disposed of on Dec. 6, and reiterated that the Egyptian Government could not agree to referral to the International Court of Justice. (Telegram 731 from Cairo, Dec. 3, noon; 984A.53/12–354)
